Avery (People Ops): Heads up — Diego Ramos received his monthly research stipend but it was processed as a non-taxable reimbursement in the US payroll run. He’s actually a US employee on a short-term foreign assignment (Portugal) so this looks wrong. Can Payroll weigh in?
Liam (Payroll): Thanks, Avery. Can you paste the paystub snippet or payroll run id? I’ll look up the journal.
Avery (People Ops): Sure — payroll run id: pr-2026-03-15-42. Paystub line: 
```nEARNINGS: Research Stipend    1000.00   non-taxable
TAXES: Federal 0.00, State 0.00
```
Liam (Payroll): Hmm — that code should have been taxed as supplemental wages. Might be a classification flag mismatch from the submit form. Might be Workday mapping. Diego, can you confirm what the stipend was for (conference travel vs living allowance)?
Diego Ramos: It was a living allowance while on short term assignment — housing support for 6 weeks in Lisbon. I filled the "assignment stipend" checkbox on the form.
Maya (HR Ops): We had a product change last quarter that split the stipend types; sometimes the older form entries still come through. @Liam could be a mapping issue between Workday -> payroll CSV.
Liam (Payroll): Okay. I’ll pull the raw import. Also need Diego’s employee id and country code used on the run.
Avery (People Ops): Employee id 49217; country code on record was PT for assignment, but payroll run flagged US for taxation. Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PR-3487
Samir (Tax Counsel): Quick note — if it should have been treated as taxable US wages, we may need to do a retro withhold and potentially issue a corrected W-2 (W-2c) for the year. If treaty or split residency applies, that affects grossing up. I’ll consult tax counsel on PT/US interplay.
Liam (Payroll): Thanks Samir. Action plan: 1) I’ll reclassify the entry for PR run 2026-03-15-42, run an off-cycle recalculation for Diego, and compute retro withholdings. 2) If net pay was already disbursed we’ll coordinate a corrective payroll. 3) If totals change for calendar year, we’ll escalate for W-2/W-2c.
PayrollBot: Payroll job pr-2026-03-15-42: import parsed, 1 record flagged for manual review (employee 49217).
Diego Ramos: Appreciate the quick help — do you know if I’ll owe anything out of pocket?
Liam (Payroll): Depends on amount withheld in the correction. We’ll provide a breakdown before we process. If company error caused the misclassification we can discuss gross-up or spread options.
Maya (HR Ops): Tagging Benefits — if housing was through vendor benefits program there may be different treatment. @Avery can you confirm vendor payments vs stipend?
Avery (People Ops): It was direct stipend via payroll, not vendor. I’ll add that to the ticket.
Samir (Tax Counsel): I’ll flag compliance implications. If we need W-2c we should start documentation now. Also check whether any state withholding (CA/MA) needs correction given Diego’s permanent state is CA but assignment was PT.
Liam (Payroll): Will do. ETA: I’ll have a preliminary calc and ticket comment by EOD today.
Avery (People Ops): Great — thanks. I’ll update Diego and add the assignment paperwork to the Jira ticket. :thumbsup: 
Diego Ramos: Thanks all — let me know if you need any forms from me.
Liam (Payroll): One more thing — if we proceed with off-cycle, expect two entries: reversal of the non-taxable and new taxed earning. I’ll post a sample before processing.
Avery (People Ops): Perfect, please cc me on the ticket updates.
PayrollBot: Ticket PR-3487 updated: payroll lead assigned -> Liam (Payroll).
